commits.message:
App asks for the kitty keyboard protocol; the parser reads its keys (#560)

* App asks for the kitty keyboard protocol where a program wants it, pushes it where the terminal answers and pops it on hand-back; the parser reads its keys by their legacy names (rich-control-codes-xh4n.anf)

* Kitty keys: an answer pushes only onto the take that asked, keypad keys type, Private Use and Super chords name nothing, Alt+Shift as legacy, no F3 from a cursor report, every reported name bindable (rich-control-codes-xh4n.anf)

* Kitty keys: keypad navigation, the shifted key reported (flag 4), quit keys checked against the app's own keyboard, a failed ask fails the app, one record per take (rich-control-codes-xh4n.anf)

* Kitty keys: shortcuts by base-layout key, one key-name set, push failure caught (rich-control-codes-xh4n.anf)

Addresses the third high pass on #560: Ctrl/Alt chords take the base-layout
subfield; parseKeyName drops its protocol parameter since decodeCSI reads
CSI u in every mode; .catch(fail) covers a throwing push write; typed()
shared by byte and kitty keys; KeyboardProtocol exported from ./host;
docs name how Ctrl chords differ under the protocol.
